title: Casper and the Provision
premise: Desert ranger Petra Coldharbour, a man who erased his past to survive, tracks a river thief and instead finds a salvage chest bearing the seal of Veymar—the drowned nation he once served and betrayed. The chest points to a wreck holding proof that could clear the name of everyone his old commanders condemned, including the woman he loved. Racing a licensed salvage fleet across six tides, Petra must choose between staying invisible and surfacing as a traitor to claim justice. He reaches the wreck at the final tide, surrenders himself to the fleet's magistrate, and trades his freedom for the truth—finding belonging not in escape, but in the crew of outcasts who refuse to leave him behind.
about_author: O. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways that no longer appear on any official chart. They write adventure fiction about people who live in the gaps between borders.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Tracking a small-time thief through salt flats, Petra corners him at the river's edge only to watch the man dive for something half-buried in the silt: a chest stamped with Veymar's seal—a nation drowned ten years ago, and the one Petra helped condemn. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine; the miles he trusted suddenly mean nothing.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with interludes from Sefa, the thief, who knows the wreck's location and hates the salvage fleet as much as she fears it. Forced into uneasy alliance, they learn the fleet's magistrate is Petra's former commander. The beat is reluctant trust: two people with buried pasts measuring each other against a shrinking clock.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Climax. Diving the flooded ruins by lamplight, Petra finds the manifest proving the condemned were innocent—and finds Sefa held at gunpoint by the fleet's advance divers. He surfaces, reveals his name and crime openly for the first time in ten years, and bargains his surrender for her life and the manifest's passage. The beat is love against duty, finally chosen out loud.

chapters.title: Coldharbour, At Last
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating Petra's and Sefa's POVs. Aboard the magistrate's barge awaiting judgment, Petra expects exile; instead the crew he'd dismissed as scavengers testifies on his behalf, and the manifest forces an inquiry. Released under Sefa's surety, he takes a place among them—not a ranger, not a ghost, but a name spoken freely. The beat is belonging earned, not granted.
